data.name: Saurav
data.gender_notes: Saurav is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Saurav is derived from the Sanskrit word 'Saur', meaning 'sun'. The name Saurav thus signifies 'Son of the Sun'. This name has a rich cultural and mythological significance in Hinduism. The name Saurav carries the meaning “Son of the Sun” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Saurav usually hope their child will grow to embody son of the sun and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A symbol of power and energy from the sun, representing vitality and strength.
data.etymology: Saurav belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Son of the Sun.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Saurav total 1, giving a life-path number of 1. Number 1 is linked with Sun and with the qualities of leadership, independence and initiative.

data.cultural_impact: The solar importance of the name is deeply rooted in Hindu culture, where the sun is considered a symbol of energy, life, and creativity. Many Hindu deities are associated with the sun, such as Surya, Ravi, and Agni. The term 'Saurav' is a reminder of this cosmic influence and the importance of the sun in Hindu tradition.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, Saurav is a name that evokes the divine energy of the sun within an individual. It is believed that those named Saurav are imbued with the strength, vitality, and light of the celestial body. The name also represent the traditional Indian virtues of courage, determination, and nobility, making it an inspiring and powerful choice for a child.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Saurav is a name derived from 'Surya', the Hindu sun god. It symbolizes the radiance, power, and strength associated with the sun. Individuals named Saurav are believed to embody these qualities, shining brightly in their personal and professional lives.

vedic_reference.note: The name Saurav is derived from the Sanskrit word 'Saur' meaning 'Sky' or 'Heavens'. It is a beautiful name with celestial and heavenly connotations.

historical_references.reference: According to Mahabharata, Saurav was a king of the Ikshvaku dynasty who ruled Haihayas in ancient India around 1200 BCE. He was the father of King Prthu, who was the first human ruler of the earth after the divine rule of the demigods.
Saurav was also a legendary king of ancient Magadha, around 6th century BCE. He is mentioned in Buddhist texts as the father of King Bimbisara, who was a major patron of Buddhism.
